clue.text: Noon, and crate's broken open for delicious drink

parts.note: N is the standard abbreviation for noon

indicators.note: a crate broken open has its contents spilled out in disorder, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word crate supplies the letters to be mixed

explanation.surface: At midday someone breaks open a crate to get at a tasty drink inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Nectar was the drink of the gods in Greek myth, and is used loosely for any delicious beverage.

clue.text: End of game inventor reviewed

indicators.note: to review is to look back over something, so the word is read in the backward direction

parts.note: Thomas Edison, the American inventor of the phonograph and light bulb

explanation.surface: At the close of a match, someone's invention is being reassessed.
explanation.walkthrough: NO-SIDE is the referee's call ending a rugby match, an old term still used in rugby circles.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby, no-side is the term for the final whistle that concludes play.

clue.text: Character cutting could be a cheat

parts.note: a card is an eccentric, amusing person, a character
a cutting remark is a sharp one

explanation.surface: Someone with a biting personality might turn out to be a swindler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting' also suggests cutting a deck of cards, which fits the answer's world.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardsharp is a professional swindler who wins at card games through trickery.

clue.text: A row about the Spanish workshop

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a word placed about another goes around it, enclosing it

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats in a theatre
el is the Spanish masculine definite article

explanation.surface: An argument breaks out over the Spanish studio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' reads as a quarrel, but it means a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: An atelier is an artist's or designer's studio, a workshop where creative work is made.

clue.text: Sailor almost in a depression? Very close

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another is surrounded by it

parts.note: taken as written
a dent is a hollow or depression in a surface

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word's final letter is dropped

parts.note: Jack, or jack tar, is a traditional name for a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman nearly sinks into gloom, and is told he is very near.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' suggests low spirits; here it is a physical hollow. The sailor loses his last letter before going in.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjacent means lying next to or bordering, so very near in position.

clue.text: Wife, after large drink, gives incomprehensible talk

parts.note: a double is a twice-sized measure of spirits
'my old Dutch' is Cockney slang for one's wife

explanation.surface: A wife who has had a stiff drink starts talking nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: Dutch for wife comes from the Cockney phrase 'my old Dutch', from 'duchess'; 'after' puts it behind the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Double Dutch is an idiom for gibberish, language that cannot be understood at all.

clue.text: One who offers counsel, as diver at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused and all over the place, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone gives guidance while working as a diver in the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: An adviser is a person whose job is to give guidance or recommendations.

clue.text: Little fish always biting line

indicators.note: something biting holds another thing in its jaws, enclosing it

parts.note: ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A small fish keeps snapping at the angler's line.
explanation.definitionFit: An elver is a young eel, a small fish migrating up rivers from the sea.

clue.text: Sweet one aboard streetcar is heading for university

indicators.note: a passenger aboard a vehicle is inside it

parts.note: a streetcar is the American name for a tram
I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of university

explanation.surface: A sweet-toothed passenger on a streetcar is travelling to the university.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiramisu is an Italian dessert, and a sweet is the British word for a dessert course.

clue.text: Show vet

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to broadcast or display a film
second meaning: to check candidates thoroughly

explanation.surface: An instruction to display an animal doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vet' is a verb here, to check, not an animal doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: To screen a film is to show it, and to screen applicants is to vet them.

clue.text: One who's got over nasty virus starts to visit other relicts

indicators.note: something nasty is bad and twisted, so these letters are mangled into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters

parts.note: opening letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Someone who has recovered from a virus goes to call on other widows.
explanation.walkthrough: Relicts is an old word for widows, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A survivor is a person who has come through an illness or disaster, having got over it.

clue.text: Firing girl taken in by lad is mistaken

indicators.note: someone taken in by another is received inside them
something mistaken is wrongly arranged, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
miss is a word for a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: A boy is wrong to think he has been fooled by a girl, leading to his sacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Firing someone from a job is dismissing them, so dismissal is the noun for being fired.

clue.text: Coach runs into box where there's a problem with actors

parts.note: a stage, or stagecoach, is a horse-drawn coach

indicators.note: something going into another ends up inside it

parts.note: to box is to fight with fists
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A trainer rushes into a theatre box where the cast are causing trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' looks like a theatre box in this surface; it is the verb to fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage fright is nervous anxiety before performing, a common affliction among performers.

clue.text: About right, worthless people causing mêlée

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it on all sides

parts.note: scum is a contemptuous term for worthless people
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Roughly speaking, it is low-lifes who start the brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About right' reads as 'approximately correct', but 'About' is the enclosing signal and 'right' is a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrum is a disorderly crowd or scramble, a synonym for a confused tussle.

clue.text: Displays (along with archbishops, perhaps) pretensions

parts.note: to air something is to display it, so airs are displays
and means along with
an archbishop is addressed as Your Grace

explanation.surface: Showing off in the company of senior clergy is mere affectation.
explanation.walkthrough: Archbishops and dukes are formally styled 'Your Grace', hence 'perhaps' for an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Airs and graces is an idiom for affected manners meant to impress, that is, pretensions.

clue.text: Causes unnecessary alarm as crow flies off

indicators.note: off means gone bad or wrong, so these letters are put out of order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A crow taking off sets off a false alarm among the other birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As the crow flies' wants to be read as a phrase, but 'as' is the link and 'off' the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To cry wolf, from Aesop's fable, is to raise a false alarm so often that real warnings are ignored.

clue.text: Monk runs as Russian leader

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
taken as written
Vladimir Putin, the president of Russia

explanation.surface: A holy man acts as head of Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Russian leader' looks like a first-letter signal for R, but it is the whole name of a president.
explanation.definitionFit: Grigori Rasputin was the Russian mystic, often called the 'mad monk', at the court of the last Tsar.

clue.text: Star in launch a pirate injured

indicators.note: something injured is damaged and bent out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A film star appears in the launch of a movie about a wounded buccaneer.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha Centauri is the nearest star system to the Sun, a bright star in the southern sky.

clue.text: Article on Heights in the Middle East from one from Luanda?

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
the Golan Heights, a plateau on the Israel–Syria border

explanation.surface: A news story about the Golan Heights, filed by someone from the Angolan capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' is part of the surface placement: the article sits on top of the heights in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Luanda is the capital of Angola, so a person from there is a native of that African country.

clue.text: Not similar to 'fizzy' ale in UK

indicators.note: a fizzy drink bubbles and churns, so these letters are stirred up

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: British beer is nothing like the bubbly stuff sold as ale elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Unalike means differing, the opposite of resembling something.

clue.text: Peak around South American capital with cross

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for around
Lima is the capital of Peru
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: A mountain summit near a Peruvian city, marked with a cross.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' looks like a container signal but gives C, from circa.
explanation.definitionFit: A climax is the high point or culmination of something, its peak.

clue.text: Phoned after parking accident

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
rang is the past tense of ring, to phone

explanation.surface: Someone made a phone call after a car-park bump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the phoning behind the parking letter. Prang is British slang for a minor car crash.
explanation.definitionFit: A prang is informal British slang for a minor collision involving a vehicle or aircraft.

clue.text: A force losing second group of elite soldiers

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: losing something means it is removed and no longer there

parts.note: steam is force or power, as in 'full steam ahead'
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A military unit loses its second-in-command and becomes a special squad.
explanation.definitionFit: The A-team is the top squad, and also the name of a fictional crack unit of ex-soldiers.

clue.text: Tries in middle of proper dummy run

indicators.note: something placed in the middle of a word sits inside it

parts.note: real means proper or genuine
a judge tries a case, that is, hears it

explanation.surface: Attempts made halfway through a genuine practice session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tries' suggests attempts, but in the legal sense a court hears a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal is a practice performance before the real thing, a trial run.

clue.text: People in authority adopting strange logo for divinity

indicators.note: adopting something means taking it in as one's own

parts.note: 'they' is the vague term for the powers that be

indicators.note: strange means odd or out of the ordinary, so these letters are reshuffled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The authorities take on an odd emblem to represent the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Divinity is the academic study of religion and God, another name for that discipline.

clue.text: Is coming back low, male in wind

indicators.note: coming back means returning the way it came, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: taken as written
to low is to moo, as cattle do
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A man returning feels down in the gale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' looks like an adjective, but it is the verb for a cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: A simoom is a hot, dry, dust-laden desert wind of Arabia and North Africa.

clue.text: Mention a bogus name

indicators.note: bogus means fake, so these letters are a false arrangement to be reworked

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is told to cite a false name.
explanation.definitionFit: To nominate someone is to put their name forward, to name them for a post.

clue.text: Animal, steer, following embarrassed female

indicators.note: one thing following another comes behind it, so the steer is placed after the embarrassed female

parts.note: an embarrassed person goes red in the face
F is the abbreviation for female
a steer is a castrated bull, an ox

explanation.surface: A beast, a young bullock, trails behind an abashed woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steer' looks like a verb, to guide; it is the noun for a bullock. 'Following' puts it after the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The red fox is the common fox of Europe and North America, a wild mammal.
